## What it is

The Access Control policy states what the organization requires for access control and who is accountable for it. It meets [AC-1](/controls/ac/ac-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 18 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Which account types are allowed on each system, and which are prohibited? | [AC-2](/controls/ac/ac-2/) | Individual, privileged, service and emergency accounts allowed with a named owner; shared and guest accounts prohibited unless the system owner approves an exception. | System owner |
| Which identity provider is the authoritative source for accounts? | [AC-2](/controls/ac/ac-2/) | The organization's central directory or identity provider, fed by the human resources system. | Chief Information Security Officer |

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet AC-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the AC-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Access Control, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (AC-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (AC-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (AC-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (AC-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (AC-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (AC-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (AC-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (AC-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the access control policy is to be disseminated</span>. (AC-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the access control procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (AC-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Account management (AC-2)

:::note[Guidance]
AC-2 makes account management a controlled life cycle: every account has a known type, an owner, an approval and a removal trigger. Each statement below maps to one lettered item of the control. Assessors test these by sampling account requests, recent departures and the last access review, so keep the records each statement implies.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall define and document, for each system, the account types allowed and the account types prohibited. (AC-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall assign one or more account managers for each system. (AC-2b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall require <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a completed access request, a signed access agreement and completed security awareness training</span></span> before granting group or role membership. (AC-2c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall record, for each account, the authorized user, group and role membership, access authorizations and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: attributes (as required) for each account <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: an expiration date for temporary accounts, and time-of-day or location restrictions where the system supports them</span></span>. (AC-2d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall create an account only after approval by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles required to approve requests to create accounts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the user's supervisor, plus the system owner or data owner for privileged roles</span></span>. (AC-2e)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall create, enable, modify, disable and remove accounts in accordance with this policy and the account management procedure. (AC-2f)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall monitor the use of accounts for activity that does not match the account's type or authorization. (AC-2g)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Supervisor</span> shall notify the account manager and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be notified <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the system security officer</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to notify account managers when accounts are no longer required <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 5 business days</span></span> when a user's account is no longer required. (AC-2h.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Human resources office</span> shall notify the account manager and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be notified <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the system security officer</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to notify account managers when users are terminated or transferred <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 24 hours, or the same day for privileged users</span></span> when a user is terminated or transferred. (AC-2h.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Supervisor</span> shall notify the account manager and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be notified <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the system security officer</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period within which to notify account managers when system usage or the need to know changes for an individual <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 5 business days</span></span> when a user's system usage or need to know changes. (AC-2h.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall authorize access only on the basis of a valid access authorization, the intended system usage and <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: attributes needed to authorize system access (as required) <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: time-of-day, day-of-week or network location restrictions, where needed</span></span>. (AC-2i)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review all accounts on the system for compliance with this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency of account review <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: quarterly for privileged accounts and at least annually for all other accounts</span></span>. (AC-2j)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall disable or remove each account the review finds is no longer authorized. (AC-2j)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Account manager</span> shall change the authenticators of a shared or group account when an individual is removed from the group. (AC-2k)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure account management processes are aligned with personnel termination and transfer processes. (AC-2l)

:::note[Guidance]
Where the organization does not use shared or group accounts, keep the AC-2k statement and note in the system security plan that none are deployed; the assessor will still ask. Evidence for AC-2l is usually an automated feed from the human resources system to the identity provider, or a documented handoff in the termination checklist (PS-4).
:::

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current access control policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current access control policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (AC-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the access control policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current access control procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (AC-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (AC-1a.1(b))

</div>
